band.why: The EUI band runs from the weighted 5th to the 70th percentile of measured site EUI for matching buildings in the 2018 CBECS (see each reference's cbecs block). CBECS is the existing U.S. stock, mostly older than any 90.1-2019 design, so the top is capped at p70: a new-code model above most existing buildings of its type points at an export or template error. Precedent for CBECS percentile targets: ANSI/ASHRAE/IES Standard 100 derives its EUI targets from CBECS at the 25th percentile per building type and climate zone. The bottom is p5, not p10, because the SmallOffice 90.1-2019 5A prototype sits near p9. A miss is reported, not enforced.
band.standard_100: ANSI/ASHRAE/IES Standard 100 EUI targets: CBECS 2012 / RECS 2015, 25th (low energy) percentile by building type and climate zone (Addendum k to Standard 100-2018)

unmet_hours_limit.source: ASHRAE 90.1 Appendix G, G3.1.2.3 (unmet load hours for the proposed and baseline designs shall not exceed 300); reported, not enforced

references.produced_by: python sim_smoke.py --reference-only --building-type SmallOffice --template 90.1-2019 --climate-zone 5A (sim/prototype.rb, then an annual run)

cbecs.survey: EIA Commercial Buildings Energy Consumption Survey 2018, public use microdata (December 2022 revision)
cbecs.filter_meaning: PBA 2 = Office; SQFTC 2-3 = 1,001 to 10,000 ft2 (the prototype is 5,502 ft2); PUBCLIM 2 = Cool, which EIA defines as ASHRAE 169-2021 zones 5A, 5B and 5C
cbecs.eui: MFBTU / SQFT (major fuels, site, gross floor area), weighted by FINALWT, kBtu/ft2 x 11.356526 = MJ/m2
cbecs.caveat: The public file is masked and its consumption perturbed for disclosure avoidance, so these percentiles differ slightly from EIA's published tables.
